omissions.description: GET /api/v1/items/{item_id} does not check ownership: any authenticated non-superuser can read any item, but the spec requires a 400 'Not enough permissions' response when a user tries to read an item they do not own
omissions.reasoning: The specification states: 'Attempt to read the created item using the access token of the second user. Verify that the response status code is 400 and the response body contains a detail field with the value "Not enough permissions"'. The code has no ownership check in read_item and returns the item to any authenticated user.

omissions.description: POST /api/v1/users/signup returns detail 'User with this email already exists' instead of the required 'The user with this email already exists in the system'
omissions.reasoning: The specification explicitly states: 'Verify the response body field "detail" equals "The user with this email already exists in the system"' for a duplicate signup attempt, but the code raises HTTPException with detail 'User with this email already exists'.

omissions.description: The password recovery email is sent via a direct HTTP POST to the mailcatcher REST API (http://localhost:1080/messages) rather than via SMTP, which is not how mailcatcher receives mail, so emails will not appear in GET http://localhost:1080/messages
omissions.reasoning: The specification requires that 'an email was actually sent to the correct recipient via the mailcatcher service (verify via GET http://localhost:1080/messages)'. Mailcatcher captures SMTP traffic; POSTing to its HTTP API is not a valid way to inject messages into its inbox, so the verification step would fail.
